column1: # Why these lines of the page's scripts do not run in the e2e tests (V3).
# uncovered lines it does not name are "unlisted", listed lines that ran
# are "stale". Line numbers as of the CI run named in ai/plans PROGRESS (V3).

column3: drawGrid's guard for a grid drawn while the RAM size and the page classes disagree: drawMaps and boot recompute the classes before they draw; only a draw from a timer in the moment between Boot with another RAM size and its recompute could hit it (a race that cannot be forced)
the ESP tag when ESP is not mapped (paging on, ESP in an unmapped page): no shipped kernel runs with an unmapped stack
pageAt's guard for a column or row outside the grid: mouse events inside the canvas always give a column and row in range (the canvas is exactly cols x cell wide); it guards the border pixel only

needs a listing with instructions of a page below the kernel, or before the kernel entry, after a fast-forward; disasm.json has no instructions below the kernel and the fast-forward always runs to the entry before code is listed
stubShift without disasm.json or with an empty one: it is only called for yellow lines, which only exist when disasm.json has instructions
diffTip's sameAt for an address past RAM: the shifted address is at most a page above a listed instruction, inside RAM for every shipped kernel and RAM size

a yellow line over all-zero memory: needs a kernel whose code is listed before it is loaded there (Debian decompressed above 16 MiB, listed at the reset vector); no suite opens such a listing and none of the kernels built here has that layout

the boxed line that had EIP inside it (mid-instruction) is always a yellow line (the relocation stub's shifted bytes); a plain line with EIP inside needs a jump into the middle of an unchanged instruction, which no shipped kernel does in its stepped part
inspect of a page past the grid: needs a picked page above a smaller RAM size after Boot, and followEip moves the pick to EIP's page right after every Boot first
the live checkbox's timer while the machine runs with a page picked: Live is off by default and no suite turns it on while running
scan without a running machine: the Scan button and the autoscan timer are disabled or stopped while there is none
the V86 constructor throwing synchronously: with any listed RAM size and the header check's no-fit guard (Boot starts nothing then) it does not throw
the emulator-loaded listener of a machine already replaced by another boot: a boot started while the previous one is still loading v86, a race the tests cannot force
the fast-forward to the kernel entry failing (its breakpoint never hit within its budget): every shipped kernel reaches its entry
resume() while no machine is ready or a reverse step is busy: the controls are disabled then; a race between Continue and Boot
Continue after stepping back to before where the JIT had run ahead (R5): reachable only with Step back after a JIT run and then Continue (not Step); suites reverse and jitrev step forward instead
a replay whose inputs end exactly as Continue resumes it (the run's end due at that count): a timing that a replay file cannot pin to a Continue
switching to stepped while v86's own loop runs (real-time clock at full speed, then a slower speed): the clock change and speed change paths pause first in every suite
resume on the virtual clock while v86's own loop is still running: the clock switch to virtual pauses v86 first
the machine replaced (Boot) while resume awaited em.stop(): a race that cannot be forced
pending JIT input slices when switching to v86's own loop: only after typed keys on the virtual clock just before the switch; a timing race
the machine replaced while resume awaited jitFlush: a race
jitLoop: the machine paused or replaced while it flushed pending inputs: a race
a replay whose next input is a mode change (the recorded run stepped from here) inside the JIT loop: replay files of the suites switch modes only while paused
jitLoop after jitExactStop reported "gone" (the run paused or replaced during the exact stop): a race
jitExactStop entered with an end already set by the slice that just ran: the slice stops at the end and the loop checks st.dead() before calling it
the exact stop's stepper loop finding the run paused or replaced between its slices: a race
pause() without a ready machine: the Pause control is disabled then; a race with Boot
driverTick after the run left stepped mode: the driver timer is cleared when it does; a timer already queued is the only way in (race)
a Run to or a counted run that reaches the initramfs prompt while stepping (not under the JIT): the Debian prompt is reached only by the JIT in the tests; stepping there takes far too long for CI
a hlt with interrupts on (waiting for the timer) while stepping: no shipped kernel idles with hlt in its stepped part (they end with hlt and interrupts off)
followEip while the JIT runs: callers only call it when paused or stepping
jumpTo an address outside RAM: every link points into RAM (EIP, ESP, symbols of the loaded kernel)
openFnSource when no DWARF frame names the function opened (a symbol name the DWARF does not know): the shipped DWARF names every symbol the Calls chart and the bookmarks open
on a phone, the function header still under the Source sheet after scrolling to its first instruction: the header is one row above that instruction, which the scroll already places in the strip
unwindHere's 4-byte read across a page boundary: stack slots are 4-byte aligned in every shipped kernel, so a read never crosses a page
EIP in an unmapped page (paging on): the CPU would fault there, so the stepper never stops with such an EIP
endText without an end: every caller calls it once stepper.end is set (markHalt, the run's "end", the panic text) or checks it first; kept as a guard
doStep without a stepper or during a reverse step: the Step control is disabled then
doStep when the machine went away while pausing: a race with Boot

Step's own 5 s check: stepper.run gets the time left as its own limit and returns "time" first; this only fires when a slice ends by count just after 5 s (the 5 s limit itself is tested: misc panic_text)
endText without an end: every caller calls it once stepper.end is set (markHalt, the run's "end", the panic text) or checks it first; kept as a guard
doRunTo without a stepper or during a reverse step: Run to is disabled then
doRunTo when the machine went away while pausing: a race with Boot
a Run to while a replay plays: the replay suite stops replays with Pause and Step only
a fast Run to aborted (Pause during the JIT to the kernel entry) that did not reach the target: a race between Pause and the fast-forward's last slice
showTip on an element without data-tip: every listener is on [data-tip] or tip marks, which always have it

tipReanchor when the redrawn listing no longer has the open popover's mark (the line scrolled out of the drawn page): needs the listing redrawn at another page while a popover is pinned, a race with stepping
a touch long press cancelled by moving more than 10 px: CDP touch emulation in the suites taps without moving
the context menu after a long press on a tip: headless Chromium sends no contextmenu for an emulated long touch
an operand that ASM_MEM does not parse as memory and that has no parenthesis: iced's GAS output gives memory operands as disp(base,index,scale) or a bare address
asmLocal for a chain without DWARF local frames: not reached by the operands suite's instructions
module.exports: runs only under Node (test_dwarf.py), which jscov does not measure
bmTargetText of an unknown kind: bmValid refuses other kinds on load, import and links
This position with no machine or before it runs: only between a kernel load's start and its boot
a call stack frame without a function start: frames carry data-fnpa only when a symbol was found
bmDraftAt of a non-element target (a text node): contextmenu and pointer events target elements
a Coverage tree function row: the bookmarks tests bookmark the file row; function rows have no bookmark step yet
the Page tab's ☆ with no page selected: the page follows EIP from the first pause or step, so selectedPage is -1 only while the first JIT run of a page loaded at full speed has not stopped
bmRenderPages without #pages_box: the element is in index.html
a page bookmark beyond the grid (made with more RAM than now): the bookmarks tests keep one RAM size per kernel
Save in the dialog with no draft: the dialog is open only with a draft
a bookmark saved before the kernel's SHA-256 is known: hashing finishes within milliseconds of the load, before a dialog can be confirmed
a pending jump older than two minutes: a kernel that does not run for 120 s (a failed fetch now drops the jump at once)
a pending jump while the machine is not ready: ticks every 300 ms, and the switch's boot in the tests is ready sooner
a pending bookmark jump for another kernel while the switched machine is not ready yet: bmPendingTick returns and retries; the tests' jumps land after the switch is ready
bmNote without #bm_status: the element is in index.html
Delete of a bookmark not in the list: each row's ✕ is for a listed bookmark and the list is redrawn on every change
a rename finished without a change (Escape or the same name): the tests rename with a new name and Enter
bmRender without #bm_list: the element is in index.html
the contextmenu event a touch long press ends with (Android): Playwright's touch emulation sends none after a long press
covRun with no stepper: the Coverage tree is drawn only after a boot creates the stepper; defensive
covExport without files.json: the lcov button is disabled while dbgFiles() is not ok, and the re-run after more shards arrive (COV.exporting) starts only from an export that had files.json
a machine-state section whose reader throws: each reads fixed fields of v86's CPU object (pinned v86 0.5.471); a throw would need a v86 build without one of them

the restored views' set trap: after a restore neither v86's JS (cpu.js writes fpu_status_word[0] only in its constructor, before the page replaces the view) nor the page writes last_result, fpu_status_word or mxcsr; the get trap is what runs (snapdiff checks the views)
a v86.wasm without the gen-v86.sh export: the site ships only the patched build (gen-v86.sh --check in CI)
a Restore while the stepper has JIT blocks pending: snapshots are restored while paused, after jitFlush already ran at the pause
a kernels.json entry without dwarf: test_kernel_data.py requires every shipped kernel to have its DWARF data
a shard fetch that fails after another kernel was chosen (mine !== DBG): a race of a slow 404 with a kernel switch
a message from a Worker of an import that was replaced (mine !== DBG): the old Worker is terminated first, so only a message already queued can arrive; a race
a Worker error of an import that was replaced: same race as line 135
dbgRestore overtaken by another kernel or import while reading IndexedDB: a race
dbgRestore overtaken while reading the units: a race
dbgRestore overtaken while reading the variables: a race
dbgRestore overtaken while reading the CFI: a race
dbgRestore overtaken while reading the locals: a race
types Worker error after an IndexedDB write of a replaced import: a race (types Worker answers after the import changed)
the locals request of one unit fails after the types pass read the same unit without error: decodeData with locals runs in both, so a unit that fails fails the types first
a unit's locals bring types the types pass did not have: both passes read the same DIEs; the merge is a guard for a table from IndexedDB of an older page version
a types table without function facts: written by an older version of this page into IndexedDB; the current page always adds funcs
dbgFunction over a function that spans two shards with the second not loaded: needs a function crossing a 64 KiB shard boundary in a shipped kernel at the time it is asked
dbgFunction with a row of no length: the line tables have no empty rows inside a function
files.json naming a shard the index does not list: both written together by gen-dwarf.js; only inconsistent data
cstrAt with no string section or an offset past it: only for corrupt DWARF (a strp/line_strp beyond .debug_str); every file in the tests has its strings
a string attribute in a form no compiler writes for names (strx forms are handled above): only corrupt DWARF
addrx/DW_OP_addrx without .debug_addr: clang always writes .debug_addr with them; only a corrupt or stripped file lacks it
DWARF 5 DW_AT_ranges without .debug_rnglists: compilers write the section with the attribute; defensive for a stripped file
DWARF 2-4 DW_AT_ranges without .debug_ranges: as above, defensive for a stripped file

root DIE whose abbreviation code is not in the table: corrupt unit header; the broken-input cases hit the code in later DIEs (bad abbreviation code) instead, a missing root abbreviation has no reader to compare with
line program that ends without DW_LNE_end_sequence: no assembler or compiler writes one; defensive against a truncated .debug_line

nameAt of a nameless DIE with DW_AT_specification but no DW_AT_abstract_origin: subprogram names through a specification are read by subRecord/decodeUnit; nameAt is asked only for origins and static locals' functions, whose specification chains (C++ out-of-class methods) carry names on the concrete DIE
abbreviation code missing among a subprogram's children (corrupt unit): defensive; the broken-input case fails earlier in decodeUnit

varargs read through subprogramAt (an abstract origin in another unit with DW_TAG_unspecified_parameters): needs an LTO build with an out-of-line varargs function in another unit; the C++ fixture's varargs come through the same unit
subCache over 50000 entries: only a huge LTO import; a memory guard
cval of a missing DW_AT_const_value: an enumerator without a value, which no compiler writes
ownExpr with an operation dwOpEnd does not know next to a DW_OP_addrx: no compiler writes such an expression
DW_OP_addrx without .debug_addr in a local's location: as line 261, defensive for a stripped file
abstract origin chain of more than one step for a local (an origin that itself has an origin): GCC and clang point every concrete DIE at the abstract one directly

a clang block without DW_AT_abstract_origin and without code whose copy differs from the origin: the case the comment describes needs a specific clang inlining pattern absent from the fixtures and the shipped kernels' checked samples
foreignKids of an offset before the first unit: not a DIE offset any reference gives
abbreviation code missing among a foreign DIE's children: corrupt unit, defensive
typeAt of an offset before the first unit: not a DIE offset any reference gives
typeAt of a DIE whose abbreviation code is missing: corrupt unit, defensive
declAt of an offset before the first unit: not a DIE offset any reference gives
declAt of a DIE whose abbreviation code is missing: corrupt unit, defensive
type key of a DIE offset that is no type DIE: a DW_AT_type pointing at a non-type (corrupt), defensive
two definitions at one address where the first known has no file: a __weak definition without DW_AT_decl_file next to the kept one; no fixture or shipped kernel has it
foreign type of an offset before the first unit: not a DIE offset any reference gives
a function whose DIE chain has no name at all: compilers name every subprogram with code (or its abstract origin); only corrupt DWARF
a function DIE with code whose name cannot be resolved (see the line above): only corrupt DWARF
a scope whose parent scope had no code (dropped): nested blocks under a block with no ranges; compilers give a block with variables code or drop it
dwScopeIn false: dwarfScopesAt asks it only for scopes that contain pa, which lie inside the previous one in every DWARF tested
an enum declaration resolved to its definition: C has no forward-declared enums in the fixtures or kernels (a GNU extension)
dwTypeSize of void: callers ask it for variable and member types, never void
dwTypeName of an unknown kind: the type table only has the kinds DWT lists
dwVarsPick by file in a types table without files (types.json of an older gen-dwarf.js): every table built now has files
dwPathIn through void: a variable or member of type void does not exist
dwPathIn into an array of elements of size 0 (an array of empty structs or of an incomplete type): none in the fixtures or kernels
a unit without cover ranges (no DW_AT_ranges or low/high_pc on the compile unit): the fixtures' and kernels' units all have them
a function range outside every PT_LOAD (discarded code, e.g. .exit.text of a vmlinux): the fixtures' code is all loaded; the shipped kernels' tables are built by gen-dwarf.js in node
dwarfFileAddrs for a table that does not name the file: dwarfFileCode asks only the tables files.json or the import's line programs list for it
a row clipped to nothing at a shard boundary: needs a row ending exactly at a 64 KiB shard edge in a shipped kernel's file code; not in the checked files
tables without is_stmt bits (MKBD version 1 shards from an older gen-dwarf.js): every shipped shard is version 2
rows of one line continuing across two tables (shards): a line whose code crosses a 64 KiB shard boundary in a file the tests ask for
a shard that is not MKBD 1 or 2: shards are written by gen-dwarf.js in CI; only a corrupt download
MKBD version 1 shard: every shipped shard is version 2
MKBD version 1 shard: every shipped shard is version 2
module.exports for node (gen-dwarf.js): never true in the browser, where coverage is measured

a type unit (DW_UT_type/split_type, -fdebug-types-section with DWARF 5) in the lines request: no fixture has type units; their references (DW_FORM_ref_sig8) are not resolved by dwarf.js, so such an import is not supported beyond file:line
a kernel without startup_32: every shipped kernel's symbols have it; only an imported symbol file lacking it reaches the _text fallback
new WebAssembly.Module() refused for a JIT block: Chromium compiles modules of this size synchronously on the main thread; the fallback is for browsers with a smaller synchronous limit
waiting for an asynchronously compiled block: only after the fallback at 83
a JIT block that fails to compile: v86 emits valid wasm
jitChunk with its budget already reached: callers pass an until past the current count
both panic lines written within one JIT slice before the exact stop: the J3 budget stops at the instruction writing the last line, so the exact end is found first
the stepped BIOS part reaching the target's code range without its address: the target is the kernel entry, first reached at its own address
save_state() failing during the fast-forward (PCI not yet set up): the 2 M stepped instructions before it (FF_STEP_FIRST) get past SeaBIOS's PCI setup for every shipped kernel
save_state() failing during the fast-forward (PCI not yet set up): the 2 M stepped instructions before it (FF_STEP_FIRST) get past SeaBIOS's PCI setup for every shipped kernel
save_state() failing during the fast-forward (PCI not yet set up): the 2 M stepped instructions before it (FF_STEP_FIRST) get past SeaBIOS's PCI setup for every shipped kernel
Pause or a new boot during a fast-forward's jitFlush: blocks compile synchronously (83), so the flush does not yield
restore_state of the slice's own save failing: v86 restores every state it wrote after PCI setup
the CPU dead before the kernel entry: every shipped kernel reaches its entry
disasm.json with no instruction starting exactly at a Run to target: targets are function starts or breakpoint addresses of the same build
a fast Run to already at its target: Run to from a target goes on to its next hit (app.js steps off it first)
the target reached while stepping until its code matches the build: the code at a target runs only once it is in place
a boot during that stepping: a race
as 351
Pause or a boot during the breakpoint run's jitFlush: blocks compile synchronously (83)
a boot during the breakpoint run: a race
and N more out-of-line copies: needs a function with more than FN_OOL_SHOWN (8) out-of-line copies among those the suites show
E1 track (genimport.js, another agent's file): a second vmlinux import while the first one's Worker still runs
E1 track: a failure of an import already replaced by another (race)
E1 track: the result of an import already replaced by another (race)
E1 track: no IndexedDB key for the import (a browser keeping no data)
E1 track: restoring kept files while an import's Worker still runs (race)
E1 track: a C source picked before the generated files arrived: the tests pick it afterwards
E1 track: indexing the picked C source failing in the Worker; no test tree makes it fail
E1 track: an index result for a pick or import already replaced (race)
E1 track: a WASI tool (llvm-nm, llvm-objdump) exiting non-zero: only for a file they cannot read, which the import refuses earlier
E1 track: an import with more than 20,000 symbols and trim auto: only Debian-sized kernels, not imported in the coverage jobs
E1 track: a vmlinux without DWARF given to the generators: the tests import -g files
E1 track: llvm-objdump failing in the Worker; the shipped tools do not fail on the test files
E1 track: the C source index asking for a shard the generated DWARF lacks: an internal invariant

the fs colour class by name prefix: the Calls tab colours by source directory first (dirOf); this name fallback is for functions without a file, and none of the shipped kernels' fs functions lacks one

buildTree's skip of frames that start before the kernel entry: frames are pushed only for symbols, and no shipped kernel has a symbol below its entry, so no frame starts before sinceEntry (checked: 0 such frames in a whole minified run)

taskInfo's walk up through a retpoline thunk frame to kthread: needs a recorded kthread frame whose child hangs below a thunk-named frame; the minified Linux has no retpolines and CI's Debian tasks run records none either

taskInfo's fallback name (kthread's last other call, without retpolines): needs a kthread whose thread function is reached neither from ret_from_fork nor through a thunk; CI's minified and Debian runs record none

drawTimeline without a stepper: graphTick returns before drawGraph without one, and G.stepper is null only when the stepper failed to install (a v86.wasm without the step exports, which the site never ships)
minimap skip of a frame that ends at or before the window start: as line 135, no frame starts before the entry, and a focused frame's descendants lie inside it

focus mode: a frame not under the focused one inside its time range at a deeper row: only a sibling starting exactly at the focused frame's end could be there; not reached by CI's focus on start_kernel and not forceable
task switch label skipped when closer than 8 px to the previous label: the minified Linux has one switch, and CI's Debian tasks run never places two labels within 8 px in the views it draws

graphRestore of a view captured with another stepper: needs Back to a Calls history entry after the kernel was booted again; a defensive guard no suite reaches (navhist keeps one boot across its entries)
timelineSummary without a stepper: a test-only helper (graph_check) always called after a run
timelineSummary's skip of frames that end before the entry: as line 135, there are none
drawTree without a stepper: as line 326 (graphTick needs one, and a tree toggle exists only in a tree drawn from one)
drawTop without a stepper: as line 326

called from unknown in the Calls info: a frame has no caller address only when the first instruction the stepper ever ran starts it; pages start at the reset vector (BIOS, no symbol) and Run to steps its last instructions, so no shipped flow records one (checked: 0 in a whole minified run, 0 after Run to hello_main and 40 steps)
a stub array symbol without a size: the shipped symbols.json give early_idt_handler_array, irq_entries_start and spurious_entries_start their sizes (checked)
removing the arcs' svg when a listing box is drawn again without arcs or stubs: not reached by the jumps walks (each listing that had arcs is next drawn with arcs)
a path whose other end has no physical address: every recorded and static transfer of the shipped kernels lands in RAM
the "no direct path" note in a list of paths into an instruction: not reached by the suites' lists (those with paths in have direct ones)
module.exports: runs only under Node (test_jumps.py), which jscov does not measure
Node only: kgen.js loading dwarf.js and unwind.js under Node (gen-dwarf.js); the page loads them as scripts
an ELF that is not 32-bit little-endian: the import refuses it before the generators run
an allocated section outside every PT_LOAD segment: not in the imported kernels
llvm-nm lines without a size: llvm-nm -nS prints sizes for the imported kernels' symbols
llvm-objdump continuing a long encoding on its own line: only with raw bytes shown; the generators ask for --no-show-raw-insn in the page
a vmlinux without CFI: the imported test kernels have .debug_frame
the function table without instruction starts (objdump failed): see genworker.js 120
a type or partial unit: the imported kernels have only compile units
a vmlinux without .debug_info given to kgenDwarf: the callers check first
a type or partial unit (see 552)
a source path outside the kernel tree (a compiler header) in the line table: the imported test kernels' paths are all in the tree
an inlined call whose file text was not shipped or has no function name: not in the imported test kernels
Node only: module.exports
iced_x86.js without its Node tail: the pinned iced 1.21.0 (fetch-v86.sh, SHA-256) has it
iced failing to load (fetch or instantiate error): the site ships it and no test blocks it
decodeLive before iced has loaded: its callers return early until iced is set
run() over an empty range or one past guest RAM: the code symbols and text sections of the shipped kernels lie in RAM with a size
inputFlush for a stepper that is not the machine's, or before inputBoot: every caller passes the current stepper after the boot set INPUT.send
inputTaint during a replay: its callers stop the replay first (replayStop in doStep, revRun, restore) or cannot run while one is active
inputReset for another stepper: the save and checkpoint paths pass the current one
a snapshot save or a JIT checkpoint during a replay: JIT checkpoints are off during replays (revJitTick) and no test saves mid-replay; the replayStop path itself is checked for Step and Step back
Restore during a replay: reachable (Restore while a replay runs) but not in a test yet; replayStop itself is checked for Step and Step back
a scancode on the real-time clock or for a replaced machine: no test types on real time
runRamHash on a mem8 whose offset in wasm memory is not a multiple of 4: v86 allocates guest RAM page-aligned in its wasm memory, so the word path always runs
replayFinish with no replay or one already done: its callers check replayActive() first
replayStop with no replay running: its callers check replayActive() first
renderRunInfo without #run_text: the element is in index.html
Download run with no run: the button is disabled whenever runNow() would be null (runNowable)
the file input's change event with no file: Chromium fires change only when a file was picked
a checkpoint due at the count of the last one: revTick runs before each slice and a slice runs at least one instruction
v86's save_state() throwing while stepping: no device of the shipped machines throws
the previous checkpoint's pack failing: the worker packs every state v86 writes

stepping at a slow-motion speed (Continue at a stepping speed) while stepped back into a JIT stretch: Step uses revStepTo there; the tests go on from a step back with Step (jitrev) or the JIT (reverse jit)
a JIT stretch and a stepped one starting at the same count: needs a mode switch with no instruction between
the stepping driver's room while stepped back with a JIT stretch ahead: as 234, Continue at a stepping speed after stepping back into a run the JIT went on with
revJitTick's branch: revJit, earlier in the same slice, already branched, so behind() is false here
revTrim with no full checkpoint after the first: the first of every group is full and trimming starts only with more than a group
the cached checkpoint trimmed away: the cache holds a recent checkpoint and trimming drops the oldest group
a delta checkpoint whose base was trimmed: revTrim drops whole groups up to the next full one, so bases go with their deltas
a boot during the worker's unpack of a checkpoint: a race
the JIT running no instruction from a running CPU: v86's main_loop always runs at least one
the CPU dead (hlt with interrupts off) during a JIT re-run: a run that ends dead stops at that instruction, which is never re-run past
as 434 for a stepped re-run
a boot during a long reverse operation's yield: a race
a reverse button while one runs or without a machine: the buttons are disabled then (revRender)
a reverse button without history: disabled then (revRender); only a click racing a revReset reaches it
a reverse operation throwing: only the defensive errors listed here (lost base, replaced machine, JIT not getting on)
Step back at the history's start: the buttons are disabled when the count is not past the first checkpoint, and the count only grows between that render and a click
a re-run partly by the JIT and partly stepped: re-runs in the tests go by the JIT to the target (jitrev); the stepped remainder needs a JIT stretch ending inside the re-run
revStepTo with nothing ahead: doStep and Continue call it only when stepped back with the JIT ahead (revNeedsJit)
revRender without #rev_info: the element is in index.html
Back to without a machine or while busy: the button is disabled then
navigator.storage.estimate() rejecting: it resolves in every secure context; Chromium offers no way to make it reject
getAll() of the snapshot store failing after open() succeeded: a browser-internal IndexedDB error (corrupt LevelDB files) that a page cannot cause
Save snapshot with no machine, before it is ready or during a reverse operation: the button is disabled in these states, only a click racing the change reaches it

a save while compiled JIT blocks are queued: blocks compile synchronously (fastforward.js jitDetInstall), so the queue is empty between the slices where a click lands; only a browser refusing synchronous compiles leaves them pending
a new boot replacing the machine during that jitFlush await: needs the queue above plus a boot in the same moment
v86's save_state() throwing or the kernel hash promise rejecting during a save: neither happens for the shipped kernels and devices
Restore while a reverse operation runs: REV.busy lasts the milliseconds of a Step back; a click in that window is a race
a rename while the Page tab is the shown tab: names are edited in the Snapshots tab, so tab is never "page" there
renderSnapshots while a name is being edited: the table is redrawn by a save, a restore, a kernel load or a delete, each started by a click outside the name field whose blur ends the edit first
a worker answer for an id nobody waits for: only after onerror cleared the waiters and a late message of that worker still arrives
Diff with a picker empty or no machine: the Diff button is disabled then (renderSnapPick)
a register missing on one side of a diff: the worker's cpuOf gives every register but EFLAGS and the meta always has EFLAGS (snapMeta); only a record from before both had them
a newer diff started while the hexdump's page was read: the worker answers in a few ms, faster than a second click
reading a page after the diff succeeded: the worker keeps both sides decoded (KEEP 2 plus now); it fails only if the worker died in between
same as 951 for the Page tab buttons
same race as 947 for the Page tab buttons
gzip records (S1) in a browser without DecompressionStream: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit all have it
a delta holding more pages than the full state: only when most of RAM changed to zero between two saves, which no kernel run does
a page read of now without its decoded RAM: now is never evicted from the worker's cache, only lost with a new worker
srcUseShipped for a kernel without "src": every kernels.json entry (hello, hello-os, both minified builds, Debian with and without its initrd) ships its source
race: another kernel loaded while index.json was being fetched; not forceable without stalling a fetch across a kernel switch
race: as line 38, the index.json fetch failed after another kernel was loaded

deref of a pointer whose own 4 bytes are past the end of RAM: every variable lies in the kernel image, which v86 loads into RAM, and a member or index step that leaves RAM ends in a value "(not in RAM)" before any further ->

a float or double value (DW_ATE_float): no global variable of the minified Linux or the Debian kernel has a floating-point type (the kernel builds with -mno-80387 and keeps floats out of its data); the dwarf_forms fixture's double is checked there (GCC fixture suite, not in the coverage jobs)

a struct or union with no definition anywhere in the vmlinux: gen-dwarf.js links every declaration to a definition when one exists, and no global of the shipped kernels (nor any pointer from one) reaches a type that stays only declared (checked: none in either types.json)
struct, union and array types nested more than 24 levels: pointers are leaves in the tree, so only nesting of aggregates counts, and no kernel type nests that deep
localStorage throwing while the watch list is saved: the list then lasts until the page closes; storage failure is tested for the stored list, not this write

localsReadBytes without a stepper CPU or for more than 4 KiB: locals are drawn only at a pause with a stepper, and no parameter or local of the shipped kernels at the unwound frames is larger than a page

localsReadBytes across a page the page tables do not map, after the first one mapped: localsPhys handles a contiguous run first, and a local that straddles a mapped and an unmapped page needs a stack at the edge of its mapping, which no CI stop has

a DW_AT_const_value given as a block (DW_FORM_block*): clang and GCC emit integer constants as data forms for the shipped kernels; the block form is in the hand-written DWARF of the dwarf_forms suite (not in the coverage jobs)

a local in memory whose bytes span two pages that are not physically contiguous: kernel stacks are physically contiguous (THREAD_SIZE pages from the buddy allocator), so no stack slot of the CI stops is split

current_task not readable: it is a global of the kernel image (or its per-CPU template, in RAM too), so the read fails only when RAM is smaller than the image, which no boot has
